documents.title: New Patient Visit / Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
23M here to set up primary care. Last regular doctor was the family practice he went to growing up; hasn't been in for a couple of years. No complaints today. Just finished the summer working as a beach lifeguard, season wrapped up last week.

PMH: none.
PSH: wisdom teeth out at 18.
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: nothing he knows of that runs in the family; specifically no skin problems, eczema, asthma or allergies on either side.
SH: single, lives in Easthampton. Never smoked, no vaping. Drinks socially, a few beers on a weekend night here and there. No drug use. Swims, runs on the beach for work conditioning.

ROS: negative.

Exam: well-appearing, fit. Vitals in flowsheet.
HEENT: TMs clear, oropharynx benign, dentition good.
Neck: supple, no adenopathy, thyroid not enlarged.
CV: RRR, no murmur.
Lungs: clear throughout.
Abd: soft, nontender, no organomegaly.
Ext: no edema, full ROM.
Skin: tanned; no atypical moles on the areas examined.
Neuro: grossly nonfocal.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 2.

A/P: healthy 23 yo, establishing care.
- Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH; one-time HIV and hep C screening, he agreed.
- Thinks his last tetanus shot was in middle school. Tdap today. Flu shot today.
- Sunscreen counseling given his job: broad spectrum SPF 30+, reapply after swimming, rash guard and hat when he can.
- Will request records from prior office.
- Physical yearly.

results.text: Positive: short hyphae and round spores ("spaghetti and meatballs" pattern)

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology group, new patient consultation
Date of visit: 03/13/2023
Referred by: primary care

Thank you for sending Mr. Holt, a 23 year old man, for discoloration of the back.

History: He describes several months of steadily increasing discolored patches on his back. He works outdoors as a beach lifeguard in the summer and notices it gets worse then, especially with heat, outdoor activity and sweating. He has no other medical problems.

Past surgical history: third molar extraction at 18.
Medications: none.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: no skin disease or atopy in the family.
Social: never smoker, drinks occasionally. Summer lifeguard.

Examination: Multiple hypopigmented macules with a fine overlying scale across the upper back. No erythema.

In-office testing: KOH prep of scale from the upper back shows short hyphae together with clusters of round spores, the classic "spaghetti and meatballs" picture.

Impression: Tinea versicolor (pityriasis versicolor).

Plan:
1. Ketoconazole 2% shampoo used as a body wash to the trunk, left on about 5 minutes before rinsing, daily for 2 weeks.
2. Explained that this is an overgrowth of a yeast that normally lives on the skin and is not contagious. The scale clears quickly with treatment, but the light color can take several months to even out, and will look more obvious after sun exposure before it does.
3. Recurrence in hot, humid weather is common. Return if it comes back.

Please contact our office with questions.

documents.title: back still looks blotchy
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I did the shampoo every day for the 2 weeks like the dermatologist said. The flaky part went away but my back still looks blotchy and white in spots. Is that normal or should I do more?

documents.title: RE: back still looks blotchy
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's expected. The shampoo clears the yeast fast, but the skin underneath takes a while to make its normal pigment again, usually a few months. If the scale stays gone you don't need to repeat it. If the flaking comes back, let me know or call dermatology.

documents.body: My summer job needs a health form signed by a doctor before I start Memorial Day weekend. Uploading it now. Do I need to come in for it or can you fill it out from my physical in September?

documents.title: RE: form for work
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Gavin, your doctor completed and signed the form using your September physical. It's uploaded to your portal under Letters, and we also left a copy at the front desk if you'd rather pick it up.

documents.title: Dermatology Follow-up
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology group, follow-up visit
Date of visit: 02/28/2024

Mr. Holt is a 24 year old man we first saw last March for tinea versicolor of the back. He comes back with a similar picture. Since a beach vacation, where he spent several days in the sun, he has noticed spots that have spread slowly over the last few weeks. They don't itch, burn or hurt. He thinks they stand out more now that he has a tan. Scrubbing in the shower has not changed them.

ROS: no recent illness, fever, sore throat or weight loss. No joint pain, no night sweats. No new medications.
Medications: none.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: noncontributory for skin or atopic disease.
Social: one sexual partner, condoms every time.

Exam: Scattered small oval flat macules over the upper chest and back, lighter than the surrounding skin, with well-defined edges. Most concentrated on the upper back. Gentle fingernail scraping brings up a fine powdery scale. No surrounding redness. Remainder of skin exam normal; hands, feet, groin and face are uninvolved. Palms and soles normal. Oral and conjunctival mucosa clear. No cervical, axillary or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

Assessment: Recurrent tinea versicolor, clinical diagnosis.

Plan:
1. Ketoconazole 2% shampoo to chest and back, 5 minutes then rinse, daily for 2 weeks.
2. Reviewed that the light patches will lag behind the scale and may take months to fill in.
3. Follow up as needed.

Thank you for allowing us to participate in his care.

documents.title: shampoo question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick question. Derm said leave the shampoo on 5 minutes but the pharmacy label just says apply daily. Which is right? Also is it ok to use it on my chest, the label says scalp.

documents.title: RE: shampoo question
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Gavin. Follow the dermatologist's directions: lather it on the chest and back, leave it about 5 minutes, then rinse, once a day for 2 weeks. It's fine to use on the body even though the box is written for the scalp.

documents.title: Dermatology Office Note
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology group
Visit 03/12/2025

HPI: 25M, followed in our practice for tinea versicolor. He had the same problem after beach travel in 2023 and 2024 and is back after another recent beach trip, with several months of light patches on the upper back and shoulders that do not tan along with the rest of his skin. No itch. Washes often and wears sunscreen and the patches have not budged. No recent illness, no medicines, no international travel.

PSH: wisdom teeth removed at 18.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: no skin or atopic disease in the family.
SH: never smoker, occasional alcohol. Lifeguard in the summer.

Exam: Upper trunk with many small, faintly scaly macules that run together into irregular hypopigmented patches, light scale throughout. No erythema. Nontender.

KOH: short curved filaments and round budding forms seen.

Assessment: Tinea versicolor, recurrent, KOH confirmed. The lightening he notices is mostly the yeast slowing the skin's pigment cells down in those spots, not damage to the skin or loss of the pigment cells, so color returns once the yeast is cleared and the skin gets some sun, typically over a few months.

Plan: ketoconazole 2% shampoo as a body wash, 5 min contact, daily for 14 days. Discussed that this tends to recur with heat and humidity. RTC prn.

documents.title: derm letter
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I saw the derm note in my portal. It says the spots are lighter because of the yeast slowing down my pigment. So is it permanent? This one bugs me more because it's on my shoulders and shows when I'm working.

documents.title: RE: derm letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Not permanent. The pigment cells are still there, they just stop working normally under the yeast. Once the shampoo course clears it, the color catches up, usually over a few months, a bit faster once you're in the sun. The yeast part can come back, which is why it has shown up each year.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, 26M.

Tinea versicolor came back again in early March after a beach trip; derm did a KOH (positive) and another 2 week ketoconazole shampoo course. He says the color on his shoulders filled back in over the late spring. Nothing on the skin now.

Meds none. NKDA. Never smoker. Alcohol occasional. Still lifeguarding summers.

Exam: vitals ok. Pleasant, well. HEENT wnl. Neck supple, no nodes or thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear to bases. Abd soft. Skin: trunk without scale. No edema.

PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 2.

A/P
- Tinea versicolor, recurrent, yearly in the spring and summer, managed by derm with topical courses. He asked about a way to keep it from coming back; told him to bring it up at his next derm visit, some people do a monthly wash in the warm months.
- Flu shot today. Declines covid vaccine this season.
- Labs: CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH.
- Tdap next due 2032.
- RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Everything from your physical is normal, including thyroid and cholesterol. Enjoy the fall.

documents.title: Dermatology Follow-up
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology group, return visit
Date of service: 03/09/2026

History: Gavin is a 26 year old man we have seen in 2023, 2024 and 2025 for discoloration of the back and shoulders due to tinea versicolor. He first noticed it a few summers ago and it now returns every year with the warm weather. It does not itch or hurt; what bothers him is how it looks, especially after time at the beach. The light patches become more obvious once he tans and have not responded to daily showers or the drugstore moisturizer he has been using. He lifeguards each summer and our summers are humid.

Medications: none currently.
Allergies: NKDA.
PSH: third molars at 18.
FH: no skin disease or atopy.
ROS: no fevers, fatigue, night sweats or weight loss.

Exam: Numerous hypopigmented macules and patches across the upper back and shoulders, a few faintly pink, all with fine dusty scale that is easier to see when scraped with a fingernail. Not tender. No erythema around them. Face, scalp, groin and extremities clear. Mucosa normal. No lymphadenopathy. Palms and soles normal.

KOH (in office): hyphae with clusters of spores, the typical spaghetti-and-meatballs appearance.

Assessment: Tinea versicolor with a clear yearly warm-season pattern.

Plan:
1. Ketoconazole 2% shampoo to back, shoulders and chest, 5 minutes then rinse, daily for 2 weeks.
2. Then once a month from May through September as prevention, since he is outdoors and sweating all summer.
3. Pigment will even out over a few months after clearing.
4. Return if it breaks through despite monthly use.

Thank you for the referral.

documents.title: Outside Note Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Derm note 3/9 reviewed. KOH positive again. Ketoconazole 2% shampoo 2 wk course then monthly May-Sept as prophylaxis. Med list updated. Can refill from here when he needs it for summer.

documents.title: refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Season starts this weekend. I finished the 2 weeks of the shampoo in March and the patches cleared up, but I'm almost out and I'm supposed to use it once a month through the summer now. Could you send a refill to my usual pharmacy?

documents.title: RE: refill
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sent ketoconazole 2% shampoo, one bottle with a refill, to your pharmacy. Once a month, same way as before: lather on, 5 minutes, rinse. Have a good season.

documents.title: Rx refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Refill: ketoconazole 2% shampoo 120 mL, 1 refill, sent electronically per PCP. Sig unchanged: monthly May-Sept, apply to trunk 5 min then rinse.
